stories.title: Betting on South Beach Luxury Shopping, Vivienne Westwood Plans to Open Store
stories.excerpt: Vivienne Westwood is finally getting serious about opening a boutique in Miami’s South Beach. Almost two years after buying the three-story property at 736 Collins Avenue and letting it sit vacant, the luxury fashion brand has submitted an application to build out the property, which dates back to 1921. The 4,356-square-foot ground-floor space would feature a store with three fittings rooms and two storage rooms. The second floor would house executive offices and meeting rooms, while the top floor would include a bridal showroom and rooftop deck. A neon sign would be mounted onto the entrance wall. The project “honors the building’s 1921 Art Deco and Mediterranean Revival heritage while introducing contemporary elements,” wrote Daniel Gabay, who runs National Permit Group and filed the proposal. The modern elements include “Florida limestone cladding, polished brass storefront and motifs, a rigid canopy reinterpreting the documented historic faux eave, a landmark pink neon signature, and the iconic Orb statue in the forecourt,” per the application, which Miami Beach Historic Preservation Board will consider next month. In 2024, the British brand paid $6 million for the 14,692-square-foot building located just a few blocks west of Ocean Drive, sandwiched between Seventh and Eighth Streets. Unlike most luxury labels of its size, it remains independent under the ownership of Vivienne Westwood’s family. The namesake designer passed away in 2022. Vivienne Westwood, the brand, is betting that high-end retail will return to the heart of South Beach. In the 1990s and 2000s, the area housed boutiques from the likes of Versace, Hugo Boss and Barney’s. But almost all shuttered, opting instead to open outposts at the Bal Harbour Shops up north and the Design District out west, which have become some of the highest-grossing upscale malls in the country. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Vivienne Westwood activating 4,356 sq ft ground-floor retail at 736 Collins Avenue, South Beach Miami after 2-year vacancy
Luxury fashion flagship signals tenant demand recovery in Miami Beach retail corridor with high-end leasing activity
Art Deco mixed-use conversion (retail, offices, bridal showroom) targets affluent coastal demographic in high-barrier-to-entry submarket
stories.summary: Vivienne Westwood is moving forward with buildout of its South Beach Miami boutique at 736 Collins Avenue after purchasing the three-story 1921 Art Deco property nearly two years ago. The 4,356-square-foot ground-floor retail space will anchor the building alongside executive offices and a bridal showroom across upper floors. The project preserves historic character while introducing modern finishes including Florida limestone cladding and a signature neon sign.
stories.impact: Luxury brand activation signals stabilizing demand in Miami Beach retail after pandemic softness; relevant as a leading indicator of affluent-focused residential absorption in South Beach and surrounding neighborhoods. High-end retail expansion typically precedes or mirrors Class A multifamily rent growth in gateway coastal markets.

stories.title: Lathrop GPM LLP Completes Move to New DC Office
stories.excerpt: Lathrop GPM LLP’s Washington, D.C. team has relocated to a new 7,000-square-foot office on the 10th floor of 1015 15th Street NW. “We’re excited to move into a new office space that provides our team members and clients with a modern, flexible environment in the heart of Washington, D.C.” said Frank Sciremammano, partner in charge of the firm’s D.C. office. The law firm, which is based in Kansas City, downsized as part of the move from nearly 16,000 square feet at the Watergate. Located in the heart of Washington, D.C.’s central business district, the firm’s new office offera convenient access to major transit hubs, government institutions and business corridors, as well as cultural and dining destinations. Newmark represented Lathrop in the new office space deal. Over the last several years, Lathrop has relocated 10 regional offices to reduce overall costs. “Our real estate strategy is focused on providing environments that enable our professionals to do their best work and deliver exceptional value to clients,” said Chief Operating Officer Courtney Landon. The post Lathrop GPM LLP Completes Move to New DC Office appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Lathrop GPM downsized DC office from 16,000 to 7,000 sq ft, relocating from Watergate to downtown 1015 15th Street
Law firm joins trend of office rightsizing and centralization; firm relocated 10 regional offices in recent years for cost reduction
Move reflects structural office contraction and tenant flight from older trophy assets in Washington DC market
stories.summary: Kansas City-based law firm Lathrop GPM relocated its Washington DC office to 7,000 square feet on the 10th floor of 1015 15th Street NW, downsizing from nearly 16,000 square feet at the Watergate. The move is part of a broader cost-reduction strategy that has seen the firm relocate 10 regional offices. The new space is positioned in DC's central business district near transit and government institutions.
stories.impact: Law firm downsizing reflects persistent office sector softness in DC; loss of large anchor tenant from Watergate property signals ongoing capital stack pressure on older office assets. Potential cascading refinance challenges and valuation compression in Washington DC Class B office, with knock-on effects on mixed-use development underwriting in the metro.

stories.title: Get to Know the Broker: Vickey Barron of Compass
stories.excerpt: Vickey Barron, an associate broker at Compass, knows how to get deals done — and all with the perfect mix of intelligence, charm, charisma and a take-no-nonsense attitude. It’s what makes her one of the best real estate brokers in the business. Barron, 69, has worked on more than 600 sales during her career and earned a slew of awards, including the Real Estate Board of New York’s Rookie of the Year award in 2001 and the board’s Eileen Spinola Distinguished Service Award in 2015. Barron has done an endless amount of million-dollar deals, but for her, the value of her job isn’t money — it’s the difference she can make in someone’s life. “People always want me to talk about commissions and big sales, and I just am a strong believer that our purpose in this role of real estate is not money and commission and who has the biggest numbers,” Barron said. “It’s really about serving people.” Commercial Observer caught up with Barron in August for a new series called “Get to Know the Broker,” where we connect with residential brokers to learn more about what makes them tick. This conversation has been edited for length and clarity. Commercial Observer: What was the biggest deal of your career? Vickey Barron: Ironically, this is not the one with the highest sale price or largest commission. In our business, there tends to be an emphasis on the commissions and money earned, but, going back to basics, we are in the business of helping people find homes and find solace. My biggest and most important deal was helping a 93-year-old woman negotiate a life estate so she could remain in her West Village townhouse after the sale took place. Sometimes we get caught up and forget that we’re all human and we age. Life has chapters, and our contributions matter. This deal had the biggest and most positive impact in my career. bullets: Profile of Compass residential broker Vickey Barron; 69-year-old with 600+ sales and REBNY awards
No concrete market data, transactions, or forward-looking signals presented in feature content
Article is purely biographical and does not address multifamily demand, supply, or capital flows
stories.summary: Commercial Observer profiled Compass associate broker Vickey Barron, a 69-year-old veteran of over 600 residential sales transactions who has earned multiple REBNY awards including Rookie of the Year (2001) and the Eileen Spinola Distinguished Service Award (2015). The article focuses on her career philosophy and approach to client service rather than specific market activity.
stories.impact: No material relevance to multifamily development underwriting, capital markets, or market fundamentals. This is a personnel/lifestyle feature with no data on rents, supply, demand, or financing conditions.

stories.title: Scottsdale Retail Center Inks $45.8M Refi
stories.excerpt: CBRE has arranged a $45.8 million refinancing for Scottsdale Towne Center, a 168,090-square-foot retail center located at 15444 North Frank Lloyd Wright Blvd., in Scottsdale, Arizona. Shaun Moothart, Bruce Francis, Doug Birrell, Bob Ybarra and Nick Santangelo with CBRE Capital Markets’ Debt and Structured Finance practice secured a 5-year fixed, full-term interest-only loan on behalf of their client. Scottsdale Towne Center is nearly 100% leased. The center is anchored by TJ Maxx, Ross and Mountainside Fitness and shadow-anchored by Target. The sponsor acquired Scottsdale Towne Center in 2021 and subsequently leased a previously vacant 50,000-square-foot space to Mountainside Fitness’s flagship location, helping increase occupancy to nearly 100% and positioning the asset for refinancing. Vestar showcases Scottsdale Towne Center on its website. The center is located at the southeast corner of Loop 101 and Frank Lloyd Wright Boulevard within Scottsdale Airpark, Arizona’s second-largest employment corridor. The post Scottsdale Retail Center Inks $45.8M Refi appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: CBRE arranged $45.8M refinance for 168,090 sq ft Scottsdale Towne Center; 5-year fixed interest-only structure
Asset nearly 100% leased with TJ Maxx, Ross, Mountainside Fitness, Target; occupancy driven by 50,000 sq ft Mountainside Fitness flagship lease (2021 onward)
Property in Scottsdale Airpark, second-largest employment corridor in Arizona; sponsor acquired 2021, positioned for refi
stories.summary: CBRE Capital Markets secured a $45.8 million, 5-year fixed interest-only refinancing for Scottsdale Towne Center, a 168,090-square-foot retail center in Scottsdale, Arizona. The asset is nearly 100% leased with anchors including TJ Maxx, Ross, Mountainside Fitness, and shadow-anchor Target. The sponsor acquired the center in 2021 and subsequently leased a 50,000-square-foot space to Mountainside Fitness's flagship location, driving occupancy to nearly 100% and enabling the refinance.
stories.impact: Retail refinancing success in Scottsdale signals stabilization of non-grocery-anchored centers with fitness/wellness tenants; relevant to mixed-use developers considering retail integration in Phoenix-area multifamily projects. Fitness-anchored retail is outperforming category average and may justify retail buildout in larger residential developments; Scottsdale Airpark's employment concentration supports co-tenancy thesis for live-work mixed-use.

stories.title: Green Street Expands Student Housing Data Platform
stories.excerpt: Investors eyeing student housing assets have a newly expanded study tool. College House, a destination for specialized data and analytics on the U.S. student housing sector, is officially offering investors and operators direct access to analytics firm Green Street’s investment analytics. The platform expansion launched on Tuesday, a little more than a year after Green Street acquired College House in 2025. The news comes amid a complicated cooling period for the U.S. student housing market, according to Green Street’s own 2026 student housing report. Asset values have declined recently due to rising cap rates, while revenue growth is expected to average just 2 percent over the next two years, slightly trailing apartments. Capital is returning to student housing, according to commercial real estate finance firm Walker & Dunlop’s annual outlook, but is similarly selective, and activity remains below 2022 peaks. Construction starts are slowing and deliveries are highly concentrated, with the market splitting along enrollment trends. College House users can now tap Green Street estimates tailored to the student housing market within its platform, including key metrics like cap rates, risk-adjusted return estimates, occupancy and supply. The announcement also introduced a proprietary scoring framework, dubbed University Grades, that identifies long-term rent growth potential for nearly 180 U.S. schools. “This is exactly the integration we envisioned when we acquired College House,” Andrew McCulloch, chief analytics officer of Green Street, said in a statement. “Combining Green Street’s independent research and proprietary valuation framework with College House’s best-in-class data assets, will provide student housing investors a complete toolkit to allocate capital more effectively.” Time for investors to hit the books. Emily Davis can be reached at edavis@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Green Street expanded College House student housing analytics platform; acquisition completed in 2025, integration launches 2026
Student housing cap rates rising, asset values declining; revenue growth expected 2% over next two years, below multifamily average
Capital returning to student housing but selective; activity remains below 2022 peaks; sector experiencing 'complicated cooling period'
stories.summary: Green Street Analytics formally expanded its College House student housing data platform, offering investors direct access to investment analytics more than a year after acquiring College House in 2025. The platform expansion launched as the U.S. student housing sector experiences a cooling period: asset values have declined due to rising cap rates, while revenue growth is projected to average just 2 percent over the next two years—below multifamily. Capital is returning but remains selective, with transaction activity still below 2022 peaks.
stories.impact: Student housing sector cooling and underperforming multifamily on revenue growth signals cap rate expansion and valuation pressure; underwriting of student housing development should assume tighter financing terms and higher discount rates. For multifamily developers with mixed student/workforce housing models, cap rate differential is widening against student segments, pushing capital allocation toward age-restricted and workforce-focused rental communities.

stories.title: Developer Eyeing 143-Acre “Italian Village” in Prosper
stories.excerpt: BlackStone Communities is prodding the town of Prosper to adopt its plans to recreate an Italian Village. The Marco, a proposed 143-acre mixed-use development, is slated for the northeast corner of the Dallas North Tollway and US 380. Community Impact reports plans for the development include a public square, retail, single-family and multifamily housing, a performing arts venue and a hotel, all centered around a lagoon with canals big enough to navigate by boat. Marco’s defining feature is its lagoon and canals, which span over 15 acres. The Marco features a mix of housing options with the total number of residential units capped at 4,400. They include: Mid-rise apartments: maximum 2,500 units High-rise residential (condominiums or apartments): maximum 400 units Retirement community: maximum 500 units The Marco also includes a significant office, commercial and entertainment component. In addition to office condos for smaller companies, conceptual plans for The Marco show two larger campuses with separate parking designated for corporate headquarters. The post Developer Eyeing 143-Acre “Italian Village” in Prosper appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: BlackStone Communities proposing 143-acre mixed-use 'Italian Village' called The Marco in Prosper, TX (Dallas North Tollway & US 380 NE corner)
Project capped at 4,400 residential units (single-family and multifamily) with 15-acre lagoon/canals, retail, hotel, performing arts venue, office campuses
Prosper location signals north Dallas suburban growth trajectory and developer confidence in corridor absorption; master-planned community scale de-risks unit delivery
stories.summary: BlackStone Communities is proposing The Marco, a 143-acre mixed-use development in Prosper, Texas at the northeast corner of Dallas North Tollway and US 380. The project features a 15-acre lagoon and navigable canals as the centerpiece, with a capped 4,400 residential units (split between single-family and multifamily), retail, office campuses, a hotel, and performing arts venue surrounding a public square. The development is in conceptual/approval phase with the town of Prosper.
stories.impact: Large-scale master-planned community in high-growth Dallas exurb signals developer confidence in north Dallas population migration and long-cycle absorption. 4,400-unit cap implies strong pre-leasing/pre-sales demand; approval timeline will signal municipal capacity and entitlement velocity in Collin County. If entitled, project will pull forward multifamily supply pipeline in Prosper submarket and may accelerate rents in established northern Dallas submarkets as renters migrate further north.

stories.title: Lone Star PACE Facilitates Nearly $65M in Loans for 6 Texas Projects
stories.excerpt: Lone Star PACE closed on $64.8 million in Texas PACE Program financing during the first half of 2026, supporting approximately $279 million in commercial real estate investment while helping property owners significantly reduce energy and water consumption. The six closed transactions span a diverse mix of property types, including hospitality, retail, industrial, data centers and specialty development, demonstrating the growing role of Commercial Property Assessed Clean Energy (C-PACE) financing in helping developers strengthen project capital stacks while incorporating high-performance building systems. Projects financed during the first half of the year include the Holiday Inn Express in Pilot Point, MCM Elegante in Beaumont (shown), Ashford Yard in Houston, Cold Storage Seabrook, Vesgro Data Center in Irving and Maranello Luxury Garages in Plano. The Texas PACE Program enables property owners and developers to finance qualifying energy and water conservation improvements through a voluntary property assessment. C-PACE financing can fund up to 35% of a project’s capital stack and may be used for new construction, redevelopment and retrofit projects. The post Lone Star PACE Facilitates Nearly $65M in Loans for 6 Texas Projects appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Lone Star PACE closed $64.8M in C-PACE financing for 6 Texas projects (H1 2026), supporting ~$279M total CRE investment
Diverse property mix: hospitality, retail, industrial, data centers, specialty development; can fund up to 35% of capital stack for new construction and retrofit
Program demonstrates third-party capital availability for energy/water conservation improvements; strengthens project economics and developer capital stack flexibility
stories.summary: Lone Star PACE closed $64.8 million in Commercial Property Assessed Clean Energy (C-PACE) financing during the first half of 2026 across six Texas projects, supporting approximately $279 million in total commercial real estate investment. The transactions spanned hospitality, retail, industrial, data centers, and specialty development. C-PACE financing can fund up to 35% of a project's capital stack and is applicable to new construction, redevelopment, and retrofit projects.
stories.impact: C-PACE availability and deployment in Texas signals third-party capital willing to fund energy/sustainability components, effectively expanding developer capital stacks and improving project IRRs. For multifamily developers, C-PACE can offset 25–35% of high-performance building system costs, allowing for green amenities (EV charging, solar, advanced HVAC) without equity dilution; particularly valuable in competitive Austin, Dallas, and Houston submarkets where sustainability amenities drive lease-up velocity and rent premiums.

stories.title: Triten Snags Refi on 342-Unit Houston Rental Community
stories.excerpt: Triten Real Estate Partners obtained refinancing for The Mill Residences, a 342-unit mid-rise multifamily community located at 2315 Navigation Blvd. in the East End of Houston, Texas. Northmarq’s Warren Hitchcock and Taylor Phillips arranged the refinance loan on behalf of Triten. Northmarq’s Hitchcock added. “Northmarq secured a creative and flexible refinance prior to final stabilization which replaced the construction loan, provided additional capital for the retail buildout, and gave Triten the runway needed to complete the property’s business plan.” The Mills Residences offers a mix of class A studio, one-, two-bedroom apartments. Amenities such as a fitness center, yoga studio, poolside cabanas and a quiet lounge equipped with high-speed connectivity designed for remote workers. Built in 2025, the multifamily community places residents at the center of Houston’s East End, providing residents with convenient access to public transit, dining, live entertainment and the area’s growing arts district.  The post Triten Snags Refi on 342-Unit Houston Rental Community appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Triten Real Estate refinanced The Mill Residences, 342-unit mid-rise in Houston East End, via Northmarq; replaced construction loan pre-stabilization
Asset delivered 2025; refi provided additional capital for retail buildout and runway to complete business plan; Class A studio/1-/2-bed product
East End location targets transit-adjacent workforce and creative professionals; includes amenities for remote work and arts district access
stories.summary: Triten Real Estate Partners obtained refinancing for The Mill Residences, a 342-unit mid-rise multifamily community completed in 2025 and located at 2315 Navigation Boulevard in Houston's East End. Northmarq arranged a creative and flexible refinance that replaced the construction loan prior to final stabilization, providing additional capital for retail buildout and the runway needed to complete the property's business plan. The asset offers Class A studios and one- and two-bedroom apartments with fitness, yoga, pools, and remote-work amenities.
stories.impact: Early stabilization and pre-lease refinance of new Houston multifamily signals strong lender appetite and demonstrates proof of concept for East End submarket transit-oriented development. Refinance at sub-stabilization reflects strong unit absorption and rent achievement; signals that Houston East End is absorbing new supply at healthy velocities and rents, validating continued pipeline growth in the corridor for other developers.

stories.title: Cybersecurity Tracker SecurityScorecard Renews 1140 Avenue of the Americas Lease
stories.excerpt: A cybersecurity risk management firm is renewing its Midtown office space, Commercial Observer has learned. SecurityScorecard signed a five-year renewal on its 8,475-square-foot space at 1140 Avenue of the Americas, owned by American Strategic Investment Company, where it has been since 2023, according to tenant broker JLL. The asking rent was not immediately disclosed, but the average office asking rent in Midtown in the second quarter of 2026 was $86.18 per square foot, according to a CBRE report. “SecurityScorecard is experiencing tremendous momentum as organizations around the world increasingly rely on our platform to manage cyber risk across their digital ecosystems,” Aleksandr Yampolskiy, CEO and founder of SecurityScorecard, said in a statement. “Renewing our headquarters at 1140 Avenue of the Americas reflects our long-term commitment to the city and provides our team with a workplace that supports continued growth, innovation and collaboration.” JLL’s Valentin Stobetsky negotiated on behalf of the tenant, while Josh Kuriloff, Matthias Li, Heather Thomas, Pierce Hance and Nicole Estevez of Cushman & Wakefield handled the deal for the landlord. “It has a premier Midtown location, outstanding transit access, modern amenities and a unique full-floor office with an expansive private outdoor terrace that enhances the employee experience,” Stobetsky said in a statement. Li echoed the sentiment that the Midtown market and the building’s premium offerings would aid the company in its expansion. C&W did not immediately respond to a request for additional comment. The landlord, which also goes by American Realty Capital New York City REIT or New York City REIT, arranged a lease at the same tower for Epic Insurance in February, when the company took 25,500 square feet. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: SecurityScorecard renewed 8,475 sq ft office at 1140 Avenue of the Americas (Midtown Manhattan) for 5 years; occupant since 2023
Cybersecurity firm citing 'tremendous momentum'; Midtown asking rent averaged $86.18/sq ft in Q2 2026 per CBRE; tenant renewal signals office stability
Class A trophy office in Midtown maintaining occupancy with high-growth tenant; renewal at market rates suggests selective flight-to-quality in NYC office
stories.summary: Cybersecurity risk management firm SecurityScorecard renewed its 8,475-square-foot headquarters at 1140 Avenue of the Americas in Midtown Manhattan for five years, where it has been located since 2023. The average office asking rent in Midtown in Q2 2026 was $86.18 per square foot. SecurityScorecard's CEO cited the company's momentum and the renewal as a reflection of long-term commitment to NYC and support for growth and innovation.
stories.impact: Tech-sector office renewal in Midtown Manhattan at or near average asking rents signals flight-to-quality and selective space take-up in premium locations; reflects bifurcation of NYC office with trophy assets outperforming secondary stock. For multifamily developers, tech office tenancy renewal in Midtown reinforces high-wage job concentration and supports near-office residential demand in Hell's Kitchen, Midtown West, and Turtle Bay; indicates continued professional-class rent-paying capacity in Manhattan.

stories.title: Arrow Adds Veteran Multifamily Lender Ari Mandelbaum to Grow Platform
stories.excerpt: Arrow Real Estate Advisors continues to ramp up its roster nearly two years after its founding. The capital markets advisory firm founded by Morris Betesh in fall 2024 has added Ari Mandelbaum, a former lender at Greystone and Dwight Capital, as a director to help grow its multifamily debt placement business, Commercial Observer has learned. “Ari brings a highly valuable perspective to Arrow given his extensive experience on the lender side of the business,” Betesh said in a statement. “His understanding of underwriting, credit and execution allows him to approach financing assignments from both sides of the table and provide clients with a deeper level of insight throughout the capital-raising process.” Mandelbaum previously held senior roles at Greystone and Dwight Capital specializing in agency and bridge loans across multifamily and other property sectors. He was at Greystone from 2011 to 2014 before a decade-long run at Dwight, where he ascended to an executive vice president role. At Arrow, Mandelbaum will focus heavily on negotiating multifamily loans while helping borrowers navigate alternative strategies. Among the multifamily deals he originated at Dwight was a $36 million bridge loan in 2023 for Latco Enterprises to refinance its Villa Annette Apartments property in Moreno Valley, Calif., CO first reported at the time. “I’m excited to join Arrow and work alongside a team with a strong track record across the commercial real estate capital markets,” Mandelbaum said in a statement. “My experience on the credit side has given me a firsthand understanding of how transactions are evaluated, structured and executed, and I look forward to applying that perspective to help Arrow’s clients navigate increasingly structured financing environments.” The addition of Mandelbaum comes on the heels of Arrow hiring Jeff Weinberg from Meridian Capital Group as a managing director, CO previously reported. Andrew Coen can be reached at acoen@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Arrow Real Estate Advisors hired Ari Mandelbaum (ex-Greystone, ex-Dwight Capital EVP) as director for multifamily debt placement
Mandelbaum brings 15+ years lender-side multifamily debt experience (agency, bridge); Arrow founded fall 2024, now scaling team
Move signals competitive market for multifamily capital advisory and debt placement; lender-to-advisor transition reflects market depth and capital flexibility
stories.summary: Arrow Real Estate Advisors, founded in fall 2024 by Morris Betesh, has hired Ari Mandelbaum as director to lead its multifamily debt placement business. Mandelbaum is a veteran multifamily lender with 15+ years of experience, including senior roles at Greystone (2011–2014) and a decade-long tenure at Dwight Capital, where he reached executive vice president level. At Arrow, Mandelbaum will negotiate multifamily loans and help borrowers navigate alternative financing strategies.
stories.impact: Formation and rapid scaling of independent multifamily debt advisory firm (Arrow) signals fragmentation of capital markets and borrower demand for lender-agnostic placement advice. Hiring of experienced lender-side operator indicates debt placement advisory is becoming a distinct and competitive vertical; suggests multifamily developers should expect more intermediaries and softer pricing/terms as capital advisors compete for deals. Broader trend of lender talent migrating to advisory/broker roles suggests financing market is normalizing post-crisis with more optionality and less bank monopoly power.
